business_problem: Meituan needed to increase throughput for growing computer-vision inference workloads, control the high infrastructure cost of running massive AI inference, and schedule long-tail services flexibly without sacrificing model accuracy or service stability.
solution_summary: Meituan reworked its vision AI inference environment into a microservices-based algorithm process that separates CPU services from other accelerator services and uses a middle-layer scheduling service to place workloads on the most suitable hardware. For low-traffic, long-tail inference workloads, Meituan runs models on 4th Gen Intel Xeon Scalable processors to reuse existing CPU resources and reduce dependence on higher-cost discrete GPUs. It then applies Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (Intel AMX), Intel Extension for PyTorch (Intel IPEX), and Intel Integrated Performance Primitives (Intel IPP) to optimize deep-learning execution, including converting multiple vision models from FP32 to BF16 to raise throughput with limited precision loss. Meituan also separates latency-sensitive online traffic from offline batch jobs and uses dynamic scaling to reallocate off-peak capacity, improving utilization and serving a range of vision AI applications such as image processing, certificate identification, QR code bike locks, package scanning, and identity verification.

solution_components.name: 4th Gen Intel Xeon Scalable processors
solution_components.role: They run low-traffic long-tail vision model inference workloads on CPU infrastructure to improve cost efficiency and throughput.

solution_components.name: Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (Intel AMX)
solution_components.role: They accelerate BF16 and INT8 matrix operations used to speed vision AI model inference.

solution_components.name: Intel Extension for PyTorch (Intel IPEX)
solution_components.role: It provides PyTorch-level software optimization so Meituan can better use Intel processor features for inference acceleration.

solution_components.name: Intel Integrated Performance Primitives (Intel IPP)
solution_components.role: It is part of the software optimization stack Meituan uses to further tune vision AI inference performance.

data_flow: Visual data from Meituan business scenarios enters a microservices-based vision AI process where a middle-layer scheduling service routes jobs to CPU services or other accelerator services. Low-traffic long-tail models are executed on Intel Xeon CPU infrastructure, optimized with Intel AMX, Intel IPEX, BF16 conversion, and dynamic scaling. Results are then used by downstream vision applications such as image processing, certificate recognition, QR code bike locks, package scanning, and identity verification.
business_outcome: Meituan improved inference throughput and online resource efficiency, cut service costs, and made vision AI resource scheduling more agile while maintaining acceptable model precision.

increased the overall efficiency of its online resources by over 3x
